A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same physics-residual conformal prediction framework. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A–N support comparison, including material relocated between versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original coverage, prediction-error and runtime comparisons, alongside residual-space evaluations on benchmark PDEs and tokamak applications.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical evaluations and reports revised evaluation times in Tables 3–5.

M1.justification: The residual score, marginal and joint calibration, convolutional finite-difference operators, and surrogate architectures are retained. Renaming PRE-CP to CP-PRE and adding the procedural walkthrough in Appendix C document the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate advection, Burgers, wave, Navier–Stokes, ideal MHD, reduced-MHD plasma modelling and magnetic equilibrium, including the existing distribution-shift comparisons. v2's discussion of ODEs and algebraic applications introduces no evaluated task.

E2.justification: Tables 3–5 retain the same deterministic, MC Dropout, Deep Ensemble, BNN, SWA-G and CP-AER comparators. Moving these comparisons into the main text and adding citations, including MacKay for BNN, does not change comparator participation.

E3.justification: Tables 3–5 relabel the error metric from L2, defined in v1 as a normalized-domain norm, to MSE while retaining its numerical entries. v2 also explicitly includes sampling, calibration and simulation-data generation in evaluation-time accounting. These are reported metric and timing revisions; the PDFs do not establish experimental reruns.

E4.justification: The discretisation comparison, boundary-condition analysis, good-versus-poor model comparison and residual case studies are retained. Additional discussion in Appendix D.1 interprets the existing discretisation analysis without adding tests.

E5.justification: Both versions already report the same ± summaries in Tables 3–5 and discuss variation across calibration sets. v2 adds no run counts, seed information, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: The runtime comparisons change substantially. For wave, Navier–Stokes and MHD respectively, CP-AER evaluation times change from 23/26/42 seconds to 2022/20026/40042, and CP-PRE from 23/34/82 to 32/134/482. This reverses CP-PRE's relative cost against CP-AER under revised timing accounting. Coverage and displayed error-column values remain unchanged; these revisions do not demonstrate same-setting speedups.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3.2 newly states that AER/STD require calibration data converging to a beta distribution. This introduces a distributional requirement absent from v1 and conflicts with the retained exchangeability-only statement. Appendix A's theorem and proof remain unchanged; the added canonical residual and autoregressive equations mainly explain existing formulations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements and conclusion retain the same core claims: model-agnostic, label-free calibration of physical inconsistency, marginal and joint residual-space coverage, and identification of unreliable predictions. The expanded abstract chiefly adds motivation.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses the inability to separate aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty and explains how inflated residual bounds under coarse discretisation can retain relative information. Section 6 expands v1's brief beyond-PDE suggestion and asserts that PDE success supports applicability to simpler systems, without new empirical validation.

D1.justification: v2 supplies an explicit code-repository address and a convolution-versus-cross-correlation implementation note in Appendix D, plus the procedural walkthrough. Conversely, replacing the old Appendix C removes its benchmark timing specification of a single A100 GPU and explicit in-/out-of-distribution definitions. Most architecture, training and sampling details are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting calibration discussion, boundary handling, uncertainty distinctions, implementation and potential non-PDE applications, and replaces some weather-modelling citations. The central positioning against physics-informed learning and existing UQ approaches remains stable; publication-metadata updates do not constitute new cited work.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the experimental narrative by integrating the former Appendix C comparisons into Section 5 and replacing that appendix with an algorithmic walkthrough. It also adds a dedicated extensions section, expands the abstract and limitations, and changes method terminology throughout.

P2.justification: Tables 2–5 move from the appendix into the main text with revised headings, captions and highlighting. v1's Navier–Stokes and MHD main-text Figures 5 and 6 become appendix Figures 20 and 24. Further figure redistribution and caption corrections substantially reorganize the evidence display without introducing new plotted experiments.

improvement.justification: The integrated comparisons, procedural appendix, explicit code pointer and fuller limitations improve accessibility and explanation. However, v2 leaves the L2-to-MSE switch unexplained, removes benchmark metadata, and adds a beta-distribution requirement inconsistent with its exchangeability-only statement. The large timing revisions use changed accounting rather than demonstrating improved model performance. These explanatory gains and reporting regressions leave the net change in overall quality uncertain.
